planting.note: Plant grafted trees in spring in well-drained soil in full sun, since this nearly sterile graft-hybrid does not come true from seed and is propagated only by grafting onto pear or quince rootstock.

directions: This odd bigeneric tree arose as a chance graft hybrid between European pear and whitebeam at Bollwiller, Alsace, sometime before 1612, and amateur fruit growers have kept it in cultivation ever since as a grafted curiosity rather than a seed-propagated crop. It produces small, rounded, yellow-skinned pomes with sweet, mild flesh reminiscent of an Asian pear, ripening in late summer on a tree that otherwise looks much like an ornamental pear with whitebeam-textured foliage. Because the hybrid is almost completely sterile, every tree traces back to grafted wood of the original clone, so growers should source scion material or nursery stock specifically labeled Shipova or Bollwiller pear rather than attempting to grow it from seed. It tolerates the same soils and pruning regime as ordinary pear and needs little special care beyond standard orchard maintenance.
sources: USDA ARS National Plant Germplasm System (GRIN)
